Definition: a prolonged form of a primary verb; to look closely at, i.e. (by implication) perceive (literally or figuratively); by extension to visit:--behold, look (upon), see. Compare G3700.
BiblicalUsage: theáomai is the word the Bible uses when it means to look closely at, to behold. In Matthew 6:1, Take heed that ye do not your alms before men. Across its 22 occurrences, the word keeps that same sense, whether the setting is promise or warning.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe seeing Christ is not the same as glancing at Him; beholding Him changes what I love. That is why I come back to theáomai whenever I need to remember what is true.
